mutations.contract: A CSS rule may not key on a confidence token alone -- `.conf--untraced` must always be scoped to the element that wears it (`.chip.conf--untraced`), or it hands its styling to whatever ELSE carries that token by inheritance.
mutations.note: Set B of HANDOFF_20260921_mutation_witness_enrollment_backlog.md, from LESSONS_20260918_visual_rules_nothing_checks.md sec 4. Same one-line find as conf-token-is-scoped-to-the-chip, on purpose: one mutation, two tiers, two different questions -- did the row's cells inherit the chip's white? (browser) versus may a rule name a confidence token with nothing to scope it? (python).
mutations.find: .chip.conf--untraced { color: #fff; background: var(--untraced); border-color: var(--untraced); font-weight: 700; }
mutations.replace: .conf--untraced { color: #fff; background: var(--untraced); border-color: var(--untraced); font-weight: 700; }
